problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 1: prove the determinant transformation identity for the three-dimensional alternating symbol, retaining the recalled determinant properties and epsilon normalization.
problems.short_topic: Alternating symbol and determinant of a 3 by 3 matrix
problems.disposition_rationale: This short but complete algebraic parent establishes the orientation factor behind pseudotensors and spatial rotations. The recalled oddness under row or column interchange and the normalization det 1 = 1 are part of the proof, not disposable preliminaries.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2: verify invariance of all four displayed Minkowski Maxwell equations under the full O(3) transformation (1), including the polar-vector, axial-vector, charge-density, and current rules.
problems.short_topic: O(3) covariance of Maxwell equations and axial magnetic field
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent tests parity as well as proper rotations and makes the determinant factor in the magnetic field transformation explicit. All Maxwell equations and every source-field transformation in (1) must remain together to establish covariance under reflections.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3: prove the determinant expression for the product of two alternating symbols and use it to derive the stated one-index contraction identity.
problems.short_topic: Products and contractions of three-dimensional alternating symbols
problems.disposition_rationale: This supplies a reusable tensor identity needed in relativistic electrodynamics and spin calculations. The determinant formula and its contracted corollary are connected stages, so retaining only the final epsilon contraction would lose the requested derivation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 4, all subparts (a)–(c): transform a projectile angle, specialize to a photon, derive the boosted stellar angular distribution, verify its normalization, and analyze the zero- and ultrarelativistic-velocity limits.
problems.short_topic: Relativistic aberration and beaming of an isotropic star field
problems.disposition_rationale: A strong special-relativity parent connecting velocity addition to photon aberration, the solid-angle Jacobian, normalization, and relativistic beaming. The isotropic distribution N/(4π), boost direction, angular conventions, and both limiting cases must be retained across the page break.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 5: prove general-coordinate invariance of the homogeneous Maxwell equation using the printed covariant transformation law for F and an arbitrary map with nonzero Jacobian.
problems.short_topic: Coordinate covariance of the homogeneous Maxwell equation
problems.disposition_rationale: The problem is a concise bridge from special-relativistic electromagnetism to differential-form covariance. Its density-valued alternating symbol and the exact pullback law for the two-form require a convention-aware derivation rather than a bare assertion that dF is tensorial.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 6: determine the optimal latitude for an Eötvös experiment.
problems.short_topic: Latitude optimization for the Eötvös experiment
problems.disposition_rationale: The one-sentence prompt does not specify the experimental arrangement, measured signal, Earth model, or criterion being optimized. Those lecture-dependent choices materially change the calculation, so the complete source parent cannot support an auditable prompt and solution without importing substantial omitted setup.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 7: verify identity, closure, associativity, and inverses for the Poincaré group.
problems.short_topic: Elementary group axioms for the Poincaré group
problems.disposition_rationale: This asks only for a routine verification of abstract group axioms and supplies no representation, spacetime action, Lie algebra, or physical consequence. It is too elementary to serve as a substantive supplementary Weinberg parent even though the named group is relevant to special relativity.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 1, subparts (a)–(b): derive relativistic coordinate-velocity addition from a Lorentz transformation and derive transverse-boost time dilation using a light clock.
problems.short_topic: Velocity addition and light-clock time dilation
problems.disposition_rationale: The two standard reminders form a coherent derivational check on Lorentz transformations rather than a formula-recall exercise. The arbitrary coordinate velocity and transverse light-clock construction should both be retained as complementary kinematic demonstrations.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2: express electric–magnetic duality covariantly with the Hodge dual, verify both vacuum Maxwell equations after the replacement, prove star squared equals minus one, and retain the magnetic-monopole footnote.
problems.short_topic: Poincaré duality of the vacuum Maxwell field
problems.disposition_rationale: This complete electromagnetism parent connects the three-vector duality to the four-dimensional Hodge star and its signature-dependent square. The normalization of the dual and the footnote explaining how charges would require magnetic monopoles are important convention and scope constraints.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3: express both E squared minus B squared and E dot B through F and use those expressions to establish their scalar and pseudoscalar Lorentz behavior.
problems.short_topic: Lorentz scalar and pseudoscalar invariants of electromagnetism
problems.disposition_rationale: The problem derives both independent electromagnetic invariants and distinguishes proper Lorentz invariance from parity behavior. It is compact but complete, and its signs must be rechecked under the binding metric and epsilon conventions.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 4, all subparts (a)–(e): derive longitudinal and transverse electromagnetic boost laws, realize constant fields with charge configurations, use electric–magnetic duality, and analyze a neutral current-carrying wire in two frames.
problems.short_topic: Lorentz transformation of electric and magnetic fields from physical sources
problems.disposition_rationale: This unusually physical derivation checks the field-strength tensor law against boosted source configurations and ends with the relativistic origin of a current-carrying wire's fields. Equation (1), the charge-scalar assumption, the admitted magnetic charge, and all five stages are linked.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 5: explain why no Lorentz boost can turn the timelike tangent of the stationary worldline into a spacelike vector.
problems.short_topic: Lorentz invariance of causal vector type
problems.disposition_rationale: Although brief, the parent demands the invariant-norm reason that Lorentz transformations preserve causal type, a foundational point that is often obscured by component calculations. The arbitrary worldline parameter and strict negative norm are part of the statement.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 6, all subparts (a)–(d), including the footnote explaining why orthogonality is required in the spacelike-sum claim.
problems.short_topic: Four-velocities, rest frames, and orthogonality on the light cone
problems.disposition_rationale: The four connected causal-vector results establish the future unit hyperboloid, rest-frame construction, and key orthogonality facts for spacelike, timelike, and null vectors. The printed counterexample footnote is essential to the hypothesis of part (c) and must be retained.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 1, all six displayed cases (a)–(f): decide which symbolic equations could be tensor equations and explain each failure of index type or placement.
problems.short_topic: Index-consistency puzzle using abstract tensor symbols
problems.disposition_rationale: The exercise is intentionally a notation game built from arbitrary decorative glyphs rather than defined tensors or a physical calculation. It can test index bookkeeping, but it is too slight and typographically fragile for the formal supplementary collection.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2, all subparts (a)–(c): prove worldline reparametrization invariance of the full charged-particle action, derive the Lorentz-force equation, and vary the background potential to obtain the trajectory's Maxwell source.
problems.short_topic: Reparametrization-invariant action for a relativistic charged particle
problems.disposition_rationale: A strong particle-dynamics parent joining one-dimensional covariance, the square-root kinetic action, minimal electromagnetic coupling, and the distributional current. The definitions of the arbitrary parameter and velocity, together with every factor of c and charge, must remain intact.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3: prove conservation of the functional current obtained in Problem 2 for worldlines without endpoints.
problems.short_topic: Conservation of a point-particle current
problems.disposition_rationale: The entire task refers to the current derived in the preceding top-level parent without restating its distributional formula, variation convention, or normalization. Because this parent contains no independent setup, extracting it would require importing essentially the result and notation of Problem 2.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 4, all subparts (a)–(d): rewrite 2+1 Minkowski space in polar and uniformly rotating Cartesian and polar coordinates, then derive centripetal force from the proper-time particle action.
problems.short_topic: Rotating coordinates, non-inertial metrics, and centripetal force
problems.disposition_rationale: The successive coordinate changes culminate in an action-based derivation of inertial force and provide a concrete equivalence-principle warm-up. The rotation matrix, polar-coordinate relation, dimensionality, proper-time normalization, and restriction to uniform rotation form one continuous calculation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 5: find the explicit coordinate transformation that maps the displayed two-dimensional Rindler metric to Minkowski form.
problems.short_topic: Rindler coordinates as flat Minkowski spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: This compact parent makes the distinction between nontrivial metric components and genuine curvature explicit. The sign convention and coordinate domains should be supplied in an adaptation so that the coordinate map is checked rather than merely guessed.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 1: take the nonrelativistic limit of perfect-fluid stress-energy conservation and derive both mass conservation and the Euler equation, retaining the Wald reference and notation warning.
problems.short_topic: Nonrelativistic limit of perfect-fluid conservation
problems.disposition_rationale: This directly connects relativistic hydrodynamics to its mass-continuity and Euler limits while emphasizing that the energy density includes rest mass. The pressure hierarchy, velocity expansion, and notation note are necessary to make the approximation controlled.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2, subparts (a)–(d), including optional (d): derive canonical scalar stress conservation, prove Maxwell tracelessness, derive its force-density divergence with current, interpret it, and connect tracelessness to the dilatation current and scale generator.
problems.short_topic: Canonical and Maxwell stress tensors, force density, and dilatation current
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent develops conservation from translation invariance and then relates Maxwell stress, source work, tracelessness, and scale symmetry. Optional part (d), including the spatial charge integral and generator statement, is still part of the printed parent and cannot be dropped.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3, all subparts (a)–(d), the intervening Polyakov action and einbein definition, and the einbein footnote: contrast parameter-dependent and reparametrization-invariant worldline actions, derive both equations, compare to other invariant actions, and take the massless limit.
problems.short_topic: Polyakov or einbein form of the relativistic worldline action
problems.disposition_rationale: Most calculations are specified, but the required comparison in part (c) refers only to unspecified 'other reparametrization-invariant actions.' A complete audited solution therefore depends on lecture material or an earlier problem set to identify the comparison action and its normalization.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 4, subparts (a)–(b), both north- and south-pole stereographic charts, the embedded-sphere definition, and the printed projection figure: write both maps and prove differentiability of their overlap transition.
problems.short_topic: Smooth atlas on the two-sphere from stereographic projection
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a complete chart-level manifold construction with an explicit overlap test. Visual PDF inspection confirms that the source includes a sphere-to-plane projection diagram labeled by the north pole, point p, and projected coordinates; a faithful redraw or equivalent geometric data is required.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 5: use the one-form transformation law to verify explicitly that the antisymmetrized partial derivative transforms as a rank-two covariant tensor.
problems.short_topic: Tensoriality of the exterior derivative of a one-form
problems.disposition_rationale: The explicit coordinate cancellation is a useful precursor to exterior calculus and demonstrates why antisymmetrization removes second-derivative Jacobian terms. The source requests the transformation proof, so replacing it with the abstract statement that dω is a form would weaken the parent.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 6, subparts (a)–(c), including optional extra part (c): derive coordinate components of the Lie bracket from its action on functions, prove their vector transformation law, and connect the bracket to the lecture definition of Lie derivative.
problems.short_topic: Lie bracket components, covariance, and Lie derivative
problems.disposition_rationale: This parent moves from an invariant derivation definition to a nontrivial coordinate transformation check and the Lie-derivative interpretation. Optional part (c) depends on the general flow definition from lecture, which should be inserted explicitly if the problem is selected.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 1: transform the constant Cartesian vector field W = partial_x into polar components, compute their partial derivatives, and then compute the metric-compatible covariant derivative in polar coordinates.
problems.short_topic: Covariant derivative of a constant vector in polar coordinates
problems.disposition_rationale: The exercise isolates the cancellation between changing components and connection terms for a geometrically constant vector. Retaining both the misleading partial derivatives and the final covariant derivative is essential to its conceptual point.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2: use the embedded unit two-sphere and its printed angular coordinates to construct the three independent infinitesimal rotation vector fields and compute all of their commutators, retaining both definitional footnotes.
problems.short_topic: Rotation-generating vector fields and their Lie algebra on the two-sphere
problems.disposition_rationale: This concrete symmetry parent derives rather than assumes the rotational Killing algebra on S2. The infinitesimal action on arbitrary smooth functions and the source's definition of linear dependence are necessary to identify the three global generators correctly.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3, subparts (a)–(b): construct a generally covariant, gauge-invariant curved-spacetime Maxwell action that reduces to its Minkowski form and vary it with respect to A to obtain the field equations.
problems.short_topic: Maxwell action and equations in curved spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent directly extends electrodynamics to a general metric and requires both symmetry principles and an action variation. A faithful adaptation must specify the field-strength definition, invariant volume element, and boundary condition used in the integration by parts.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 4: start from the inhomogeneous coordinate transformation of the Christoffel connection and verify explicitly that the printed covariant derivative of a one-form transforms as a rank-two covariant tensor.
problems.short_topic: Cancellation of non-tensorial terms in the covariant derivative
problems.disposition_rationale: This is the standard explicit proof that the connection's bad transformation precisely cancels the second-derivative term from differentiating a covector. The source assumes the connection transformation law, so that full law must be supplied if the parent is reused.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 1: prove that contraction of the metric-compatible covariant derivative reproduces the displayed invariant-volume divergence formula for an arbitrary vector field.
problems.short_topic: Equivalence of connection and invariant-volume divergence formulas
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent reconciles two independent constructions of covariant divergence and requires the determinant–Christoffel identity. Its metric-compatibility assumption and the source's shorthand square-root determinant convention must be made explicit under Weinberg notation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2, subparts (a)–(b): compute all nonzero Riemann components of the round two-sphere of radius r0 and integrate its scalar curvature over the whole sphere to show radius independence and obtain the number.
problems.short_topic: Gauss–Bonnet integral on a round two-sphere
problems.disposition_rationale: This provides a concrete curvature calculation whose integrated result exposes a topological invariant. Visual PDF inspection confirms that the factor r0 squared multiplies the entire parenthesis containing both angular terms; that grouping was ambiguous in extracted text and must be transcribed from the PDF.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3, subparts (a)–(c), including optional component counting: count independent Riemann components, prove the universal two-dimensional curvature form, and compare it with Problem 2's sphere result.
problems.short_topic: Algebraic form of the Riemann tensor in two dimensions
problems.disposition_rationale: The component count and one-dimensional space of curvature tensors yield the full two-dimensional formula. Part (c) explicitly depends on the preceding sphere computation, but that dependency is local and can be made self-contained by inserting Problem 2's metric and curvature result rather than omitting the check.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 4: for a particle in the printed spatially flat FRW metric, show that conjugate energy is not conserved and derive all three conserved quantities.
problems.short_topic: Particle energy and conserved spatial momenta in FRW spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: This compact geodesic problem cleanly contrasts broken time-translation invariance with the three spatial translation symmetries of flat FRW. The arbitrary scale factor and exact particle action or normalization should be stated so the meaning of conjugate energy is unambiguous.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 5, subparts (a)–(b), together with the full exponential-map construction and domain assumptions: prove connection coefficients vanish at the base point in normal coordinates and prove the Bianchi identity there and hence tensorially everywhere.
problems.short_topic: Riemann normal coordinates and the Bianchi identity
problems.disposition_rationale: The source supplies a careful exponential-map definition, including geodesic completeness and local-domain qualifications, before using normal coordinates in a curvature proof. Those global and local caveats are part of the setup and should not be replaced by the slogan that Christoffels vanish at a point.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 6, all subparts (a)–(c), including the ball-topology footnote: construct a covariantly constant coframe in a zero-curvature neighborhood, integrate it to coordinate functions, and use a linear transformation to make the metric constant canonical form.
problems.short_topic: Vanishing Riemann curvature implies local metric flatness
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a rigorous local-flatness proof rather than a coordinate example, with curvature as the integrability condition for a parallel coframe and the Poincaré lemma as the coordinate step. The simply connected ball-topology assumption is essential to part (b).

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 1: expand the printed finite metric transformation under x-tilde = x + epsilon and derive the covariant infinitesimal metric variation, retaining the distance-invariance footnote and its chain-rule explanation.
problems.short_topic: Infinitesimal coordinate transformation of the metric
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent derives the metric Lie derivative or gauge transformation directly from its finite tensor law and carefully distinguishes evaluation at x from x-tilde. The footnote's invariant-line-element argument and the sign convention for the active or passive transformation are indispensable.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2, subparts (a)–(b): for the improved stress tensor defined by metric variation of a scalar-matter action, derive its coordinate-transformation variation and use action invariance plus the scalar equation of motion to prove covariant conservation.
problems.short_topic: Diffeomorphism Ward identity for stress-energy conservation
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a clean action-based proof of covariant stress conservation. It explicitly relies on Problem 1's infinitesimal metric transformation; selection therefore requires inserting that one-line result and fixing the source's determinant and metric-variation sign conventions rather than silently assuming it.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3: prove that the Einstein tensor vanishes identically in 1+1 dimensions and explain the resulting absence of metric dynamics and matter constraint.
problems.short_topic: Identical vanishing of the Einstein tensor in two dimensions
problems.disposition_rationale: The problem uses the special algebraic form of two-dimensional curvature to reveal a dimension-dependent limitation of Einstein's equation. A full solution should derive the Ricci proportionality and distinguish the classical field-equation statement from possible topological action effects.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 1, subparts (a)–(e), including optional general-D part (d), the cosmological-action sign footnote, both AdS coordinate forms, and the explicit z-to-y transformation.
problems.short_topic: Anti-de Sitter space as a negative-cosmological-constant solution
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent varies the Einstein–cosmological action, computes the Poincaré-patch Einstein tensor, fixes Λ versus L in four and arbitrary dimensions, and transforms to a warped coordinate. The sign-memory footnote and dimensional conventions are necessary to audit every coefficient.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2, subparts (a)–(c), all introductory remarks, and both hints: compute the Einstein tensor for the spatially flat FRW ansatz, derive the positive-cosmological-constant scale-factor equation, and solve for the de Sitter metric.
problems.short_topic: de Sitter expansion from the FRW Einstein equations
problems.disposition_rationale: This directly derives cosmological-constant-driven exponential expansion from the Friedmann ansatz. One remark and Hint 2 refer to the preceding AdS warped form; a selected version must restate that equation or its Wick-rotation observation so the complete hint remains accessible.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3, subparts (a)–(c), including the Lie-derivative derivation footnote: prove equivalence of Killing's equation and metric invariance, derive the conserved stress current, and construct its time-independent charge on constant-time slices.
problems.short_topic: Killing symmetries, conserved stress currents, and charges
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent links geometric symmetry to a local current and then to a global conserved quantity. The Lie-derivative reminder, stress-tensor conservation hypothesis, choice of time slicing, induced measure, and boundary-flux assumption are all needed for a complete derivation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 4, subparts (a)–(c), the minimally and curvature-coupled scalar actions in arbitrary n, the local Weyl transformation of both metric and field, and the full Wald curvature-rescaling identity (4) in footnote 3.
problems.short_topic: Conformal scalar coupling and improved traceless stress tensor
problems.disposition_rationale: This substantial action problem computes the original trace, fixes the curvature coupling required for local Weyl invariance in arbitrary dimension, and derives the improved traceless tensor. The reproduced Wald transformation formula makes the parent self-contained and must be retained with its dimension-dependent coefficients.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 1: calculate the gravitational-radiation energy-loss rate of an equal-mass binary whose two stars have mass M and instantaneous separation 2r.
problems.short_topic: Quadrupole energy loss from an equal-mass binary
problems.disposition_rationale: The one-line prompt specifies masses and instantaneous separation but not an orbit, velocities, eccentricity, stress-energy model, quadrupole formula, or averaging prescription, so it is not actually equivalent to a fully specified circular-binary parent. Its intended calculation depends materially on omitted lecture assumptions.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 2, all subparts (a)–(e), both constant-proper-acceleration hints, the Rindler coordinate transformation, frequency comparison, equivalence-principle derivation, and causal-horizon discussion.
problems.short_topic: Uniform acceleration, Rindler coordinates, redshift, and coordinate horizons
problems.disposition_rationale: This complete equivalence-principle parent derives uniformly accelerated hyperbolae, constructs comoving Rindler coordinates, computes the metric and light-frequency shift, and interprets the missing Minkowski wedge causally. The covariant acceleration definition and both hints are essential scaffolding.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 3, including its heading on printed page 1 and full statement on page 2: recover the Newtonian inverse-square Earth–Sun force from the displayed Schwarzschild metric and calculate the first general-relativistic corrections in the small quantities.
problems.short_topic: Newtonian and first relativistic force terms from Schwarzschild motion
problems.disposition_rationale: The problem directly connects exact Schwarzschild test-particle dynamics to the Newtonian force and its leading corrections. A faithful adaptation must define which velocity and compactness quantities are expanded and derive a coordinate-invariant observable rather than treating coordinate acceleration alone as physical.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Problem 4: compute proper times from rest at finite radius to the Schwarzschild horizon and singularity, compute Schwarzschild coordinate time to the horizon, use conservation laws, and retain the explicitly imprecise finite-size tidal-force bonus request.
problems.short_topic: Radial infall times and finite-size tidal forces in Schwarzschild spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: The radial-infall core is strong, but the indivisible source parent explicitly labels its final finite-extent tidal-force request 'imprecisely-formulated' and supplies no body model, frame, orientation, or tidal observable. A unique complete solution cannot be audited without materially rewriting that required bonus part.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 5: prove that the Lie bracket of any two Killing vector fields is again a Killing vector field.
problems.short_topic: Closure of Killing vector fields under Lie bracket
problems.disposition_rationale: This concise result establishes that infinitesimal isometries form a Lie algebra and can be proved cleanly using Lie derivatives and their commutator. A full solution should state the smoothness and flow assumptions rather than presenting only an index manipulation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 6: compute the Ricci tensor for the displayed pp-wave ansatz, prove the vacuum equation is the transverse Laplace equation, and verify the tracefree quadratic profile solution, correcting only the source's mistaken equation-number cross-reference.
problems.short_topic: Exact pp-wave solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations
problems.disposition_rationale: The metric, vacuum reduction, and tracefree quadratic waveform make a compact exact-wave parent that complements linearized theory. The sentence 'show that (4) is solved' plainly refers to displayed equation (3); this typographical correction must be recorded rather than propagated.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 7, including its heading on printed page 2 and statement on page 3: for the repeated Poincaré AdS metric with z positive, prove that an inward-directed light ray reaches z = 0 in finite coordinate time and retain the boundary-condition interpretation.
problems.short_topic: Timelike conformal boundary of Poincaré anti-de Sitter space
problems.disposition_rationale: This parent distills the causal reason AdS evolution needs boundary conditions and includes the full metric and coordinate domain. The null-geodesic derivation and the interpretive boundary statement must remain together; the title alone begins on the preceding page.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 8, all subparts (a)–(c): derive the regular Euclidean period for the general conformally weighted simple-zero metric, specialize to Euclidean Schwarzschild and planar AdS black holes, and reproduce it from the printed surface-gravity definition.
problems.short_topic: Euclidean regularity, surface gravity, and black-hole temperature
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent unifies removal of a conical defect with Hawking temperature and an invariant surface-gravity calculation, then tests two geometries. The simple-zero condition, regular nonvanishing conformal factor, shrinking-circle vector, and both specialized metric functions determine all numerical factors.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 9: derive energy-momentum conservation equations for an ideal gas in an FRW universe and give their physical interpretation.
problems.short_topic: Ideal-gas energy-momentum conservation in FRW cosmology
problems.disposition_rationale: The one-sentence prompt supplies neither the ideal-gas stress tensor nor its equation of state, thermodynamic variables, particle-number law, FRW metric convention, or which independent conservation equations are intended. Those omitted model choices prevent a unique, source-auditable complete solution.

problems.parent_scope: Complete optional Problem 10, all subparts (a)–(e): vary the Einstein–Maxwell action and fix its coefficient, solve the electric conformastatic ansatz via a harmonic function, impose asymptotic flatness and charge flux, take the AdS2 times S2 near-horizon limit, and retain the magnetic-charge extension.
problems.short_topic: Extremal Reissner–Nordström solution and its AdS2 times S2 throat
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a substantial exact-solution parent that derives rather than quotes the extremal charged black hole and connects charge normalization to its near-horizon throat. The action normalization, electric ansatz, flat three-metric Laplacian, flux definition, and optional magnetic extension all require convention-aware treatment.
